turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Sit down, Hale. I have twenty minutes before a client call, so I'll be brief. Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of class. Explain that.
Get it over with, then. You haven't told me why nobody called me before that zero went in. Start there.
Look, your son cheated. Everyone knows it. I'm not wasting my evening on this.
My child never lies. Say that again and I'll be writing it down. On what basis do you say he cheated? Show me the document.
You lawyers think you can bully anyone.
I'm not bullying you, Hale. I'm asking for the document that shows Owen cheated. Who else has seen this, and was Owen heard before the zero went in?
Are you going to keep wasting my time?
You asked for this meeting, and I'm here because you put a zero in my son's gradebook without calling me. Answer the question: was Owen heard before that happened?
